**Scope.** per account, per Region.

When a declarative policy is in use, you can't modify the settings directly within an account."

**Write it as.** `a minimum of one minute` · `as soon as its state changes to stopping` · `The instance billing hour doesn't change`

**Scope.** per instance; minimum; Amazon EBS-backed instances for stop/start and hibernate.

> "Billing | The instance billing hour doesn't change | You stop incurring charges for an instance as soon as its state changes to `stopping`. Each time an instance transitions from `stopped` to `running`, we start a new instance billing period, billing a minimum of one minute every time you start your instance. | You incur charges while the instance is in the `stopping` state, but stop incurring charges when the instance is in the `stopped` state. Each time an instance transitions from `stopped` to `running`, we start a new instance billing period, billing a minimum of one minute every time you start your instance. | You stop incurring charges for an instance as soon as its state changes to `shutting-down`" (columns: Characteristic | Reboot | Stop/start (Amazon EBS-backed instances only) | Hibernate (Amazon EBS-backed instances only) | Terminate)
> — [Amazon EC2 instance state changes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-instance-lifecycle.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-10.

### ec2-stopped-instance-type-change

**Claim.** While an instance is in the stopped state you can modify certain attributes of the instance, including the instance type; you are charged for EBS storage but not for instance usage.

**Write it as.** `modify certain attributes of the instance` · `Charges are incurred for the storage` · `including the instance type`

**Scope.** stopped EBS-backed instances.

> "You are not charged for usage or data transfer fees for your instance when it is `stopped`. Charges are incurred for the storage of any Amazon EBS volumes. While your instance is in the `stopped` state, you can modify certain attributes of the instance, including the instance type."
> — [Amazon EC2 instance state changes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-instance-lifecycle.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-10.

### ec2-terminated-instance-cannot-recover

**Claim.** You cannot connect to or recover a terminated instance; it stays visible in the console for a short while and is then deleted automatically.

**Write it as.** `You can't connect to or recover` · `visible in the console for a short while`

**Scope.** terminated instances.

> "After you terminate an instance, it remains visible in the console for a short while, and then the entry is automatically deleted. You can also describe a terminated instance using the CLI and API. Resources (such as tags) are gradually disassociated from the terminated instance, therefore may no longer be visible on the terminated instance after a short while. You can't connect to or recover a terminated instance."
> — [Amazon EC2 instance state changes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-instance-lifecycle.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-10.
